The tell that it might be: the two size-matched partitions, state (15,343) and education (13,371), give nearly IDENTICAL mean benefit (-0.0032, -0.0028) while their gradients differ in sign. This run caps every site at exactly 800 records in all five partitions, so they differ only in which people are grouped together. PREDICTION: the mean benefits CONVERGE -- spread below 0.003 against the uncapped 0.011 -- while the gradients continue to differ, because size sets whether merging helps and carving sets the shape within a partition. That is a WEAKER claim than R75's and I expect it to win. If instead the mean benefits still differ widely at matched size, carving is causal for the level too and R75's strong form survives on a second population. CONFOUND NAMED: capping changes prevalence across partitions, 0.269 to 0.396, because different carvings retain different people. Rows, site size and prevalence cannot all be held fixed across different partitions at once.
